newsitem.title: CHINA: China hopes to see end to Iraq sanctions soon.
newsitem.headline: China hopes to see end to Iraq sanctions soon.

text.p: China wants to see an end to United Nations sanctions against Iraq as soon as possible, Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen told visiting Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz on Monday.

"The settlement of the problems at an earlier date is in the fundamental interests of the people in the Gulf region, and the peace, stability, and unity in the region," the Xinhua news agency quoted Qian as saying.
China appreciated Iraq's stand of continuing cooperation with the United Nations, and hoped the U.N. departments would accelerate the process of inspecting Iraq's arsenal, Qian said.

He said he also hoped the United Nations would "objectively and justly appraise Iraq's efforts to carry out relevant resolutions of the U.N. Security Council in order to ease and gradually lift the sanctions on Iraq", Xinhua said.
China wanted to advance ties with all Arab nations, Qian said.

Aziz said he hoped China, as a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council, would play an active role in the council in making contributions to the peace and stability in the Gulf region, Xinhua reported.
